The Tolupan, also called Jicaque, are an Indigenous people of Honduras. They once lived along the northwest coast and the valleys inland from it; today most live in the department of Yoro and in the mountain community of Montaña de la Flor in central Honduras. Their language, Tol, forms a small family of its own.

During Spanish rule and after independence, missions and settlers pressed them, and in the 1800s some families fled into the mountains of Montaña de la Flor, where the Tol language is still spoken. They farm maize and beans in the hills. Neighbours: Pech and Lenca.
